title: Simon Willison covers Clinejection — 4,000 dev machines via prompt injection in AI triage bot (secondary wave)
summary: Simon Willison just posted about the Clinejection attack: a GitHub issue title injected a prompt into Cline's AI triage bot, which then poisoned the npm release pipeline — compromising ~4,000 developer machines. Secondary coverage wave hitting today (daily.dev, modelslab, byteiota) means this is trending NOW.
suggested_angle: A GitHub issue title. That's all it took to compromise 4,000 developer machines via a prompt injection in an AI triage bot that had no permission boundary. The agent read the issue, interpreted it as an instruction, and executed. PP's permission layer is the gate between 'agent read something' and 'agent did something'. This is the clearest possible demonstration.

title: Agent Commander launches — 'Industry's First Platform To Detect, Protect, and Undo AI Risks To Data'
summary: New entrant Agent Commander positions as a risk detection + remediation platform for AI agents, framing the barrier to enterprise agent adoption as data risk management rather than permission governance. Focuses on detect-and-undo rather than pre-action authorization.
suggested_angle: Agent Commander's framing: detect and undo AI data risks AFTER they happen. PP's framing: authorize BEFORE the action so there's nothing to undo. The market is bifurcating into reactive (monitoring/remediation) vs. proactive (permission routing). PP owns the proactive lane. Write the piece that names this split.
